initial.name: bash
initial.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$AVN_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. A foreground command still running after 20000ms is handed back as a background job instead of blocking the turn. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way except through the escalation the denial offers. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe: run it rather than assuming the denial.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

output_files.description: For commands generating deliverables (PDF, DOCX, spreadsheets, images, etc.), list every output path here. Paths resolve against workdir. Verified new or changed files appear in the created/edited-files block. Requires foreground execution.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: create_worktree
initial.description: Create a git worktree on a new branch and move this session into it. Use it when a task needs its own checkout: work in parallel with another agent on the same repository, try a change without touching the main working tree, or leave a build in place while starting something else. The new checkout is created from HEAD, or from the revision you name; uncommitted changes in the current checkout do not carry over. Every later file, shell, and search call resolves against it, and file writes are confined to it. Subagents already get their own worktree automatically.

name.description: Worktree name: letters, digits, dots, dashes, or underscores. The branch and the checkout directory both use it. Omit for a generated name.

from.description: Revision the new branch starts from: a branch, tag, or commit. Defaults to HEAD of the session's repository.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit existing UTF-8 text files by replacing literal text. Several files whose edits are already decided go together in one call through files.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Required unless files is given.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly. Required unless edits is given.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match. Required unless edits is given.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

edits.description: Several replacements for this file in one call, applied in order; none applies unless all match. Use instead of old_string/new_string.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches of this old_string.

files.description: Several files in one call, applied in order, each file at most once. Use instead of the top-level file_path and its replacements.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly. Required unless edits is given.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Required unless edits is given.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false.

edits.description: Several replacements for this file, applied in order; none applies unless all match.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches of this old_string.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: exit_plan_mode
initial.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: git_branch
initial.description: List, create, switch, or delete branches. Switching refuses while the checkout has uncommitted changes unless allow_dirty is true, because a switch would otherwise carry or block them unpredictably. Deleting refuses an unmerged branch unless force is true.

operation.description: What to do: list every local branch, switch to one, create one, or delete one.

name.description: Branch name; required for switch, create, and delete.

from.description: Revision a created branch starts from. Defaults to HEAD.

allow_dirty.description: Switch even though the checkout has uncommitted changes.

force.description: Delete a branch that is not merged.

initial.name: git_commit
initial.description: Record the staged changes as a commit. Pass paths to stage those paths first, or omit them to commit exactly what the index holds. The message goes to git verbatim, so keep it to one clear subject line and, when useful, a body after a blank line.

message.description: Commit message, passed to git verbatim.

paths.description: Repository-relative paths to stage before committing; omit to commit the index as it stands.

initial.name: git_diff
initial.description: Show a unified diff of this session's repository. By default it compares the working tree with the index, so it shows what is not staged yet; use staged to compare the index with HEAD, or range for two revisions such as "main..HEAD". A long diff is cut and marked truncated.

path.description: Repository-relative path to diff; omit for the whole checkout.

staged.description: Compare the index with HEAD instead of the working tree with the index.

range.description: Two revisions to compare, such as "main..HEAD". Takes precedence over staged.

initial.name: git_log
initial.description: List recent commits in this session's repository, newest first, with hash, author, date, and subject. Use it to see what landed before changing history or writing a commit message.

limit.description: How many commits to report. Omit for the configured default.

initial.name: git_merge
initial.description: Merge a branch or revision into the checked-out branch. A merge that conflicts returns the paths left with conflicts instead of raising only an exit status; abort discards an in-progress merge.

ref.description: Branch or revision to merge into the checked-out branch.

abort.description: Abort an in-progress merge instead of starting one.

initial.name: git_remote
initial.description: Fetch from a remote or push the current branch to it. Omit remote to use the branch's own remote and omit branch to push the branch that is checked out. The command's own output is returned.

operation.description: Fetch remote updates, or push the current branch.

remote.description: Remote name; omit to use the branch's own remote.

branch.description: Branch to push; omit to push the checked-out branch.

initial.name: git_status
initial.description: Report the repository this session works in: checked-out branch, upstream and commits ahead or behind it, and every changed path with its staged and unstaged change. Start here before committing or switching branches.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes, the timeout expires, or the user sends a message; an unfinished wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

initial.name: ralph
initial.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

initial.name: read
initial.description: Read UTF-8 text files and return line-numbered content. Several files you already know you need go together in one call through files.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend. Required unless files is given.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

files.description: Several files in one call, read concurrently and returned in order. Use instead of the top-level file_path, offset, and limit.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

initial.name: read_aloud
initial.description: Turn spoken read-aloud of your replies on or off for this session. Switch it on when the user wants to hear the answers — language practice, pronunciation, or a hands-free conversation — and off when they ask you to stop. It changes only the reader; your replies themselves stay text.

enabled.description: true to read your replies aloud from now on, false to stop reading them.

initial.name: read_image
initial.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Aeven validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

initial.name: remove_worktree
initial.description: Remove a git worktree created by create_worktree or for a subagent, once its branch is merged or no longer needed. Without a name, removes the worktree this session works in and moves the session back to the repository's main checkout. Fails while the worktree has uncommitted changes. With delete_branch, also deletes its branch, which git refuses while the branch is unmerged.

name.description: Name of the worktree to remove, as its directory and branch name it (without the branch prefix). Omit to remove the worktree this session works in.

delete_branch.description: Also delete the worktree's branch. Git refuses while the branch is not merged.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: str_replace_editor
initial.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

initial.name: subagent_fork
initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the subagent and returns its result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

initial.name: web_fetch
initial.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text. Runs no JavaScript, so a page that builds itself in a browser may return little or nothing.

initial.name: web_search
initial.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read or change this session's working directory. With no path, report the current directory. With a path, resolve it (absolute, or relative to the current directory), require an existing directory, and make it the directory every later file, shell, and search call resolves against. The change lasts for the rest of the session; there is no directory stack to pop.

path.description: Directory to enter: absolute, or relative to the current working directory. Omit to read the current directory.

initial.name: write
initial.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
